title: Governance, Risk Assessment and the Training Programme
summary: For the Manager in Charge, Compliance Officers, Board Directors and Owners: roles, the enterprise risk assessment, policy approval, employee risk and running the training programme including professional development.

lessons.title: Roles and responsibilities
lessons.body:
## Who is responsible for what

- **Board or Owners**: approve the AML/CFT program and policies, set the risk appetite, give the Compliance Officer independence and resources.
- **Manager in Charge**: ensures the program is applied in all branches.
- **Compliance Officer**: runs the program day to day. The role is limited to AML/CFT tasks and **not combined with other functions**, to avoid conflict of interest.
- **Alternate Compliance Officer**: covers absence.
- **Compliance Committee**: gives additional oversight.

*Training summary of the CBUAE Rulebook. Always check the current Rulebook text and your own policy manual.*

lessons.title: Video: When to file a suspicious activity report under UAE AML law
lessons.body:
## Before you watch

Boards and owners must know when reports are due and who files them. Watch this short explainer, then check it against your own reporting procedure.

## Look out for

- What triggers a report
- Who is responsible for filing it
- The risk of delay or of tipping off

## After watching

Answer the short quiz to move on.

*This video is made by a third party and opens on YouTube. It is not produced by Data Mine Labs or the CBUAE, and it may describe rules from other countries. Where it differs from the CBUAE Rulebook or your own policy manual, follow those.*

lessons.title: The enterprise risk assessment
lessons.body:
## Six steps

1. Define the **scope**.
2. **Identify** risks.
3. Assess **inherent risk**.
4. Evaluate **controls**.
5. Work out **residual risk** (inherent risk minus controls).
6. **Mitigate**.

Cover **customers, products and services, delivery channels, new technologies, geography, counterparties** and sanctions and proliferation financing exposure.

Senior management must review and approve the **risk appetite statement, methodology and findings at least annually**, and after major changes. A risk assessment of a **new technology** is done **before** asking the CBUAE for approval.

*Training summary of the CBUAE Rulebook. Always check the current Rulebook text and your own policy manual.*

lessons.title: Policies and procedures
lessons.body:
## Written, approved, current

Policies and procedures are approved by the **Manager in Charge, the Compliance Officer and the Board** (or Owners and Partners if there is no Board) and are **reviewed at least annually**.

They must:

- Apply consistently to **all branches and affiliates**.
- Define **roles**.
- Require **EDD** for all high-risk customers and transactions.
- **Prohibit tipping off**.
- Describe **record keeping** in enough detail.

*Training summary of the CBUAE Rulebook. Always check the current Rulebook text and your own policy manual.*

lessons.title: Managing employee risk
lessons.body:
## Know your employee

People can be a weak point. The LEH applies **recruitment checks** proportionate to the role and verifies backgrounds before employment. It manages **conflicts of interest** of AML/CFT staff.

Warning signs include:

- A lifestyle that the salary does not explain.
- Reluctance to take leave.
- An employee linked to an **unusually large number or value** of transactions, who may be pressured or may have agreed to bend the rules.

*Training summary of the CBUAE Rulebook. Always check the current Rulebook text and your own policy manual.*

lessons.title: Running the training programme
lessons.body:
## A programme, not a one-off

- **Onboarding** within 30 calendar days. No independent customer service until passed.
- **Annual refresher** for staff who deal with customers, products or services.
- **Event-driven** training after changes in law, CBUAE notices, internal policy, or audit and risk findings.
- **Role-based content**: Board members focus on compliance culture, frontline staff on red flags.
- **Periodic testing** and repeat sessions based on results.
- **Compliance team**: per the CBUAE's continuing professional development requirement, at least **48 hours of external AML/CFT training every 12 months** (for example ACAMS-type certification, workshops or regulator sessions).
- Keep the **training register** for inspection.

*Training summary of the CBUAE Rulebook. Always check the current Rulebook text and your own policy manual.*
